result.architecture_summary: At the frozen commit, only the planning foundation is productionized: a one-time, human-approved 37-record task graph and a deterministic read-only `taskcontrol` CLI. RAG freshness, project scanning, graph mutation/reconciliation, ticket supervision, worktrees, Unity batch validation, recovery, and continuous scheduling remain future architecture. The Unity project itself is a small prototype centered on one canonical scene and one 446-line Editor scene builder; tests exist, but there is no repository-owned Unity runner, CI workflow, build pipeline, or machine-readable current runtime evidence.
result.verdict_reason: The core principles—durable state outside the model, bounded workers, Git isolation, evidence-based completion, runtime feedback, and bounded repair—are sound. The current organization is not yet sound as an autonomous Unity production pipeline because it productionized global planning before the executable Unity delivery loop. `taskcontrol ready` reports design/dependency readiness without proving that Unity, required packages, serialization, tests, or the target platform are available. The supposedly living graph has no completion/update/reconciliation-diff commands, GDD changes cannot invalidate affected work, and the planned RAG source is already stale. Reorganize around one Unity-validated gameplay vertical slice before building Milestone 2 as currently scoped.
strong_decisions: Integrated repository state, rather than worker self-report or historical assignment output, is treated as implementation truth.
Reconciliation snapshots are separated from the living task graph; an LLM cannot silently rewrite operational work.
The pipeline explicitly learned that static evaluator success cannot approve interactive Unity behavior. Human runtime failures can fail a task and re-enter refinement as structured evidence.
No-op refinement detection and bounded circuit breakers address a real false-success/infinite-loop failure.
Parallel workers and automatic merge are deferred until single-ticket reliability exists.
Unity is configured for Force Text serialization and Visible Meta Files, and every current asset inspected has a paired `.meta` file.
The canonical gameplay scene is distinguished from two non-canonical stub scenes, preventing misleading scene evidence.
Exclusive resource keys correctly recognize scenes, Input Actions, ProjectSettings, and the shared scene builder as non-merge-safe surfaces, even though enforcement is not implemented yet.
structural_flaws: Milestone ordering is inverted for production leverage: Unity compile/EditMode/PlayMode/runtime validation is Milestone 4, after a broad RAG/scanner/decomposer/artifact-authority milestone. Unity validation is the first missing prerequisite for reliable gameplay delivery.

`taskcontrol ready` means only `open + executable kind + single_agent + dependencies complete`. It has no environment, package, Unity-version, build-target, stale-canon, claim, or validation-profile gate. Several reported ready tasks are not runnable autonomously in the present environment.
The persistent graph is not operationally living. `taskcontrol` only supports validate/list/show/ready/graph; there is no supported mark-complete, stale, supersede, reconcile-diff, or apply workflow.

GDD authority is conflated. The GDD contains product design, runtime architecture, development-agent ownership, pipeline policy, token budgets, and current repository observations. Those concerns are also copied into ADRs, project requirements, task criteria, and RAG chunks.

The proposed RAG foundation is already stale: its metadata and chunks describe a July 30 GDD while root canon was revised August 21. Its 20 tests pass because they check the stale corpus internally, not freshness against the canonical file.
Tasks cite mutable headings and copied prose rather than stable requirement IDs or a GDD revision/hash. A later wording or behavior change cannot be mapped deterministically to affected tasks.

The Unity scene architecture is a throughput choke point. Thirteen of 25 implementation records lock both the same 446-line builder and the same 2,300-line scene. Resource locks prevent collisions but serialize most visible gameplay work.

The Editor tests call `DoorPrototypeSceneBuilder.Build()`, which opens and saves the committed canonical scene. Validation can therefore mutate the artifact being validated, create serialization churn, or absorb unrelated scene roots. Tests should build into an isolated temporary scene or inspect a previously generated canonical scene read-only.

The current PlayMode tests instantiate isolated components and manually invoke `Tick`; they do not exercise the canonical scene, actual Input System actions, serialized references, click movement, camera/input integration, or a build.
There is no Unity executable, host runner, CI workflow, Windows build automation, TestResults XML, screenshot/video capture, or clean-tree-after-test check in the repository.

Worktree strategy omits Unity-specific operations: independent Library directories, cold import/package-resolution cost, licensing, platform modules, one-Editor-per-project locking, and how generated serialization changes are returned from the host to the worker branch.
Exclusive-resource metadata is not reliably complete. For example, NSC-024 requires both `manifest.json` and `packages-lock.json` to change but locks only the manifest.

The global planning pipeline is disproportionately large for the game: compared with the initial Unity commit, Pipeline/Tasks/AI-pipeline documentation add roughly 99,000 lines while Assets add about 3,840. Reconciliation alone contains 158 files and about 7.3 MB.

The verified graph still contains semantic duplication, such as two nearly equivalent movement-suspension acceptance criteria in NSC-003 and duplicated schedule-fallback project requirements. Deterministic validation cannot detect this kind of contract noise.
observed_failure_solutions: Camera static passes followed by two Unity runtime failures: structured runtime feedback and human PlayMode inspection directly solved a real project failure.
A Refiner reported success while making no Assets change: observed-delta checking, failed-progress accounting, and the circuit breaker directly solve this real failure.
Historical Assignment 5 completion claims could become stale: reconciliation against the integrated checkout and serialized scene evidence solves that real provenance failure.

The first reconciliation candidate produced 21 material findings: independent coverage/evidence/scope review and bounded refinement corrected actual defects in that generated candidate, though these were planning-pipeline defects rather than shipped-game defects.

Verification experienced timeouts/interruption and conflicting field repairs: immutable runs, resume/recovery, deterministic validation, and conflict arbitration address failures created by the reconciliation machinery.
Windows checkout versus Linux-container Git status disagreement was experienced and addressed by the frozen commit's Docker Git configuration.
hypothetical_failure_solutions: Exclusive-resource locks, claims, worktrees, and future scheduling mainly protect against future multi-worker scene/prefab/meta conflicts; no dispatcher currently enforces them.
Artifact Authority and Artifact GER protect against future AI invention, but the persistent graph contains zero artifact records and no real artifact flow has exercised the design.
The proposed Unity YAML/GUID scanner protects against likely production failures, but no deterministic scanner exists yet and no historical GUID-loss incident is shown.
GitHub Issue/Project/PR synchronization, leases, merge queues, and continuous scheduling solve future operational scaling problems, not the present single-ticket bottleneck.
Project-level budgets and continuous backlog replenishment are future safeguards; only bounded per-repair retries have current evidence of value.
Fifteen-auditor reconciliation verification protects against another global bootstrap failure, but ordinary gameplay work does not need this machinery.
overengineering: A 15-auditor, multi-model, two-pass verification system with streaming field repairs and conflict arbitration for a 37-task prototype backlog.

Multiple immutable reconciliation candidates, raw outputs, current pointers, approval manifests, bootstrap markers, refined deltas, verification summaries, and duplicated Markdown renderings exceed the audit needs of this project.
Building generic Progressive Decomposition, artifact authorization, generation, promotion, and multiple artifact evaluators before one real artifact is needed.
Layering Planner, Implementer, Validator, GER Evaluator/Refiner, fresh diff reviewer, reconciliation verifier, and human approval without first measuring which roles improve one gameplay ticket.
Planning 30–40 tasks and 217 structured criteria/validation requirements before proving a repeatable Unity compilation and PlayMode path.
A generalized cached scanner/context platform is premature; a small task-specific manifest for NSC-003 would reveal the required scanner queries empirically.
missing_components: A pinned Unity 6000.1.8f1 host runner with required platform modules and documented licensing/setup.
A single command that imports/compiles, runs EditMode and PlayMode tests, emits XML/logs, performs serialized-reference/GUID checks, and fails on unexpected working-tree mutations.
A read-only canonical-scene integration test and a separate explicit scene-generation command; validation tests must not overwrite the canonical scene.
A real input/scene PlayMode test using the Input System for NSC-003, including click destination, hold steering, shared pointer projection, suspend, restriction, and reset.
A Windows Standalone build smoke test from the registered canonical scene.
A durable evidence manifest bound to task ID, commit, Unity version, package-lock hash, test artifacts, build result, and human playtest disposition.
Graph commands for approved task edits, completion, stale/superseded state, GDD-impact application, and deterministic reconciliation diff/apply.
Stable requirement IDs with revision history and an explicit many-to-many requirement-to-task/test mapping.
A freshness check that rejects RAG/index data whose canonical-file or per-requirement hashes do not match current canon.
Runtime capability gating so planning-ready work is distinguished from dispatchable-on-this-host work.
A Unity-aware worktree policy covering separate Library directories, package import caching, project locks, and merge-time revalidation.
Prefab/component ownership seams that reduce reliance on the single scene builder and canonical scene.
state_and_authority_concerns: Necessary boundaries are: accepted product requirements, technical ADRs, operational work, integrated repository state, transient execution state, and validation evidence. These should remain distinct.

The GDD should own player-facing intent and accepted design, not live repository inventory, agent orchestration policy, token budgets, or current scene facts. Technical ownership belongs in ADRs; repository observations are derived evidence.

Tasks should be executable contracts pinned to requirement revisions and a baseline commit, not independent copies of canon. Newer requirement revisions should make affected contracts stale automatically.
The RAG index is a derived cache and must never be called canonical without a verified source hash. At this commit it is an outdated authority copy.
`Tasks/*.yaml` correctly owns durable work identity, but only if changes can be applied through a supported workflow. Manual file editing is currently the only post-bootstrap mutation path.
GitHub should remain a projection of transient execution state rather than a second task-definition authority.

Bootstrap repository evidence is appropriately labeled as historical, but `taskcontrol show` exposes only that bootstrap state. A future context builder must not mistake it for current implementation evidence.

`outputs/current/STATUS.md` still says human approval is required even though the graph was subsequently approved and seeded. The docs warn that this view is non-authoritative, but the stale convenience state demonstrates the cost of duplicated status surfaces.
Completion should require merge plus a validation manifest for the merged commit. `main` alone proves integration, not that the required Unity evidence was produced.
gdd_iteration_concerns: The repository history shows repeated GDD changes through August 21, including control, ownership, navigation, restart, and Frost Field clarifications. Treating the approved bootstrap as enduring correctness is therefore unsafe.
After a GDD change, do not rerun global reconciliation by default. Parse the change into stable requirement revision events and identify linked open, in-progress, and complete tasks/tests.

Affected open work should become `stale_needs_replan`; in-progress branches should pause at the next safe checkpoint and receive a requirement diff; completed work should either remain valid with renewed evidence or create a focused change/regression ticket.

Removed or superseded requirements should preserve historical task identity but prevent obsolete work from dispatch. New requirements should produce explicit proposed graph changes requiring the appropriate design authority.
Unchanged tasks should continue. A whole-file GDD hash is useful for freshness detection but insufficient for targeted invalidation.
Playtest tuning decisions should be captured as small approved parameter/design revisions, not trigger full roadmap reconstruction.
Changes to technical architecture or pipeline policy should update ADRs, not masquerade as game-design changes that force gameplay reconciliation.

Synchronization with evolving canon is a continuous impact-analysis process. The existing reconciliation machinery is framed primarily as an audited snapshot/bootstrap process and lacks the implemented impact/apply path required after bootstrap.
result.throughput_assessment: Current near-term leverage is low and may be negative. The graph saves roadmap reconstruction effort, but it has not shortened the critical path from task selection to a validated Unity change. Most activity from August 18–21 built planning/review infrastructure, while only the camera feature materially advanced Assets. Thirteen tasks collide on the same scene/builder, Unity validation is manual, and no worker can independently prove compilation or runtime behavior. The architecture could create major leverage after a reliable one-ticket Unity loop exists, but there is no evidence yet that the current milestone sequence can turn weeks into days.
human_intervention_points: Approve design changes, tuning values, architecture changes, scope cuts, and any artifact allowed to extend canon.
Install/license the pinned Unity editor and Windows build support, and resolve package-manager or platform-module failures.
Inspect scene, prefab, Inspector, animation, imported-art, and serialized-reference changes before merge.
Playtest movement feel, combat readability, camera framing, room tactics, audio/visual feedback, and balance; these cannot be approved from source tests alone.
Resolve nontrivial scene/prefab/meta conflicts and decide how non-canonical stub scenes are handled.
Review and merge PRs until automated Unity evidence and merge safety are proven reliable.
Perform final Windows build smoke testing and delivery inspection.
Answer small design ambiguities when implementation would otherwise invent player-facing behavior.

next_slice.title: Deliver NSC-003 through a real Unity-validated vertical slice
next_slice.why: NSC-003 is already dependency-ready, exposes the first visible gameplay change, unlocks spells, doors, restart, and victory, and touches the exact risky Unity surfaces—Input Actions, Editor builder, serialized scene, runtime input, camera plane projection, and PlayMode behavior. It will reveal the minimum useful context/scanner requirements while solving the first production blocker: trustworthy Unity validation.
deliverables: A task-specific context manifest assembled from NSC-003, current GDD sections, current scripts, Input Actions, local GUID mappings, builder, and canonical scene—without building a generic scanner or RAG service.

Mouse click-to-destination and hold-to-steer movement through Input System actions, one shared cursor-to-gameplay-plane result, and owner-controlled restriction, suspend/re-enable, and reset interfaces.
Updated Input Actions, builder/scene wiring, controls UI, and serialized canonical scene with preserved `.meta` GUIDs.
Refactored builder tests that do not save over the committed canonical scene.
Real PlayMode coverage using Input System test input plus a canonical-scene serialized-reference smoke test.

A host-side Unity command that compiles, runs EditMode and PlayMode tests, emits machine-readable results/logs, verifies no unintended asset changes, and optionally produces a Windows development build.
A compact evidence manifest bound to the commit, followed by one explicit human movement-feel and scene-inspection gate.
next_slice.proof_of_value: From a clean isolated worktree, one bounded worker produces the feature; the pinned Unity host imports it, compiles it, regenerates the scene only through the authorized command, passes EditMode/PlayMode tests, leaves no unexplained diff, produces a Windows development build or documented platform failure, and yields a human-approved merge candidate. Measure elapsed wall time, human minutes, retries, context size, and failure causes.

do_not_build_yet: Generic full-project RAG/context/scanner platform beyond what NSC-003 directly needs.
Progressive Decomposer and Artifact Authority/GER until a real near-frontier design gap requires an artifact.
More global reconciliation auditors, refinement layers, output formats, or bootstrap provenance machinery.
GitHub Projects synchronization and broad issue mirroring.
Parallel coding workers, merge queue, or automatic merge.
Continuous backlog replenishment and autonomous infinite scheduling.
Roslyn indexing or incremental project-state caches.
Prefab-wide concurrency scheduling before prefab ownership seams and single-ticket Unity reliability exist.

alternative_architecture.description: Use a thin vertical-slice pipeline. State: keep stable, revisioned product requirements separate from technical ADRs; maintain a small operational backlog whose tasks cite requirement revisions and baseline commits; keep transient runs outside task definitions. Planning: select one player-visible slice, perform targeted requirement/repository impact analysis, and create only the next executable contract. Execution: one restartable coordinator, one isolated worktree, one bounded coding worker, checkpoint commits, and no generic multi-agent crew unless measured evidence warrants it. Validation: run cheap Git/scope checks, then pinned Unity import/compile, isolated EditMode tests, real scene/Input PlayMode tests, serialized GUID/reference checks, and a build smoke; add semantic diff review afterward. Recovery: preserve branch, commit, context/evidence hashes and normalized failures; allow at most a small repair budget, then escalate. Unity integration: use an explicit host Editor command for scene/prefab generation, prevent tests from changing canonical assets, split reusable systems into owned prefabs/config assets, and retain human gates for scene inspection and game feel. GDD changes enter as requirement revisions that mark linked tasks stale or create focused change tickets instead of launching full reconciliation.
alternative_architecture.why_better: It retains the sound state and safety principles while collapsing duplicated authority and moving the real production bottleneck—Unity evidence—to the front. Every infrastructure addition must shorten or secure a real gameplay delivery, stale canon becomes mechanically visible, recovery is commit-based, and scene/prefab conflicts are reduced structurally instead of merely serialized by locks.

evidence.observation: The implemented CLI supports only validate, list, show, ready, and graph. Readiness checks only status/kind/execution scope/dependencies.
Unity batch/runtime validation is deferred to a later milestone and described as eventual work on the real development machine.
Two camera versions passed static evaluation but failed human Unity runtime testing; a later Refiner also reported success with no Assets changes.
The final automated result is `accepted_static`, discloses Unity as unavailable, and relies on subsequent human rebuild/testing rather than preserved machine test output.
RAG metadata identifies a July 30 document and contains 39 old chunks, while the canonical Markdown is revised August 21. Current movement/cursor contracts are absent.
All 20 Python retrieval tests pass against the stale corpus because no test compares the corpus to the current canonical file/hash.
The GDD has repeated history changes and combines product design, runtime architecture, agent workflow, repository scene evidence, token budgets, package choices, and build/pipeline constraints.

The ready movement contract touches Input Actions, the shared builder, and canonical scene and contains two semantically overlapping suspend-interface criteria, but no GDD revision/hash or stable requirement IDs.
Package configuration requires resolved `packages-lock.json` evidence but declares an exclusive lock only for `Packages/manifest.json`.
Multiple EditMode tests invoke `DoorPrototypeSceneBuilder.Build()`, which opens and saves the committed canonical scene.
PlayMode tests create isolated GameObjects and manually drive `Tick`; they do not load the canonical scene or exercise real input/serialization integration.
A single 446-line Editor builder owns the canonical scene. Thirteen implementation tasks lock this builder and the same scene.
Unity serialization mode is Force Text.
Version control mode is Visible Meta Files; inspection found paired `.meta` files for all current Assets entries.
The project is pinned to Unity 6000.1.8f1, but no Unity executable is present in the review environment.
No scene is registered in Build Settings, so there is currently no buildable canonical-scene path.
The successful bootstrap verification used 15 parallel auditors, initially found 56 findings/21 material findings, then ran streaming field repair and conflict arbitration.
The mutable current view still says human approval is required although approval and bootstrap manifests now exist, demonstrating duplicated status drift.
Unity Library/Temp/Logs are correctly ignored, but there is no documented per-worktree Library/import/licensing strategy.
No CI workflow exists at the frozen commit.

result.biggest_uncertainty: The repository cannot show the developer's external Windows Unity installation, license/platform modules, or informal editor workflow; those could reduce setup time, but they do not supply the missing committed automation and evidence contracts.
